top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) asks a first-order question about who bears the adjustment costs of trade and technology. It does so with transparent local-labour-market designs that have been replicated and challenged for about a decade. The central finding, that adjustment was slow and concentrated in particular places, has survived in qualified form, while long-run magnitudes and shift-share identification remain contested. Credit is the tightest on the shortlist because the three jointly authored the core programme. A citation limited to exposure, employment, wages and adjustment, with no effect size and no ruling on who originated the task framework, avoids the Katz/Acemoglu/Levy-Murnane attribution problem. I do not treat the broad convergence on P001 as evidence of merit, since much of it came from members revising during round 1. I rank P002 (Helpman, Melitz) second because it is mature and cleanly credited as a two-name award, but the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum priority question, the 2008 overlap and structure-dependent welfare claims are unresolved. P000 is last because P001 clears the maturity and attribution bar. I moved to P001 from B018 only after concluding that no three-name B018 credit can be defended against the omitted contributors.
recusal_note: No tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Helpman or Melitz is apparent from my profile. Disclosures: my capital-skill complementarity and investment-specific technological change work (with Ohanian, Ríos-Rull, Violante, Greenwood and Hercowitz) is adjacent to the skill-premium strand of B036 that the proposed citation does not credit. I co-author frequently with committee colleagues Hassler and Boppart. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
